Agenda Amended 12/15/2020

  CITY OF SAN GABRIEL
  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING AGENDA

  Tuesday, December 15, 2020 - 6:30 P.M.

  City Hall Council Chamber
  425 South Mission Drive
  San Gabriel, California 91776
  Due to Executive Order N-25-20 Members of the Council may
  Teleconference into the meeting.
  Denise Menchaca  Mark Lazzaretto
  Mayor  City Manager

  Chin Ho Liao  Keith Lemieux

Pursuant to State and County Directives, San Gabriel City Hall is closed to the public and physical access
to the meeting has been suspended. To provide members of the public access to the meeting and an
opportunity to comment on items on and off the Agenda, the following opportunities have been
established:

Public Comments

Please email all public comments to cityclerk@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line of
your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, New Business) and Item Number you
are commenting on. The Clerk will read public comments into the record for up to the three-minute limit.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and discriminatory language, will
not be read.
Example: PUBLIC COMMENT: New Business Item A

   City Council Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, December 15, 2020

  •  CALL TO ORDER
  •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Harrington
  •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Menchaca, Vice Mayor Liao, Council Members Ding,
  Harrington, Pu

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 17, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of December 1, 2020.
  3. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of December 1, 2020.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – NOVEMBER 2020

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 15, 2020  2
   This is the presentation of City investments for the month of November 2020.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for November 2020.

  D. RESOLUTION NO. 20-66 ESTABLISHING CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTION
  LIMITS PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTIONS 85301 AND
  83124

  Assembly Bill 571, effective January 1, 2021, will establish individual campaign
  contribution limits for local agencies which have not adopted their own
  regulations. The City Council will consider a resolution establishing campaign
  contribution limits in accordance with state limits.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 20-66
  establishing campaign contribution limits pursuant to Government Code
  Sections 85301 and 83124.

  E. AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICE AGREEMENT TO NORTH STAR LAND
  CARE FOR CITYWIDE STREET TREE MAINTENANCE SERVICES

  The Public Works Department is responsible for the maintenance of the City’s
  urban forest, consisting of approximately 8,000 public street and park trees.
  Our in-house staff responds to residential customer service requests for tree
  pruning, removal of dead or diseased trees, and emergency hazardous branch
  and tree removals. However, in order to comply with the Joint Powers
  Insurance Authority’s recommendation that the City maintain a four-year
  tree-pruning cycle, we require a supplemental outside tree maintenance
  contract. We are also unable to reach the tallest trees with our own
  equipment. Five tree maintenance companies submitted their Request for
  Proposals by the October 22, 2020 deadline. North Star Land Care was
  determined to be the lowest responsible bidder.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 15, 2020  3
   1. Authorize the City Manager to execute a three-year Professional Services
  Agreement with North Star Land Care.
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his/her representative to extend the term
  for up to two (2) additional years in one-year increments.
  3. Authorize the issuance of a Purchase Order to North Star Land Care in the
  amount not to exceed $97,800 for services provided in the current fiscal
  year from the Gas Tax (Tree Maintenance) account 136-800-02-22-000
  and General Fund account 121-800-05-22-056 (Tree Maintenance
  Contractual Services).

  F. LEASE-PURCHASE OF A 2021 FORD F-150 PICK-UP TRUCK

  The Public Works Department is responsible for the maintenance of all the
  City’s streets and the public right-of-way. The new F-150 truck will be a
  general purpose vehicle for transporting staff, tools and materials, assisting
  in closures and detours, field investigations, and responding to emergencies.
  The truck will also free up a pool vehicle, which was originally assigned to the
  Engineering Division for field investigation and inspections.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive formal bidding and authorize the Cooperative Purchase Agreement
  consistent with the piggyback bidding requirements pursuant to
  Municipal Code Section 34.35; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with National
  Auto Fleet Group in the amount not to exceed $28,466.48.

  G. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE

  The City Council unanimously passed the budget for Fiscal Year 2020-2021
  on June 23, 2020. However, due to the staggering economic impacts of
  COVID-19, the City Council requested that staff conduct a monthly update at
  the regularly-scheduled second meeting of the month. This standing item
  would be for the purposes of bringing any major changes or developments
  to the City Council.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 15, 2020  4
   5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. 414-420 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD PLANNING CASE NOS.
  ZC19-001 (ZONE CHANGE/PLANNED DEVELOPMENT OVERLAY ZONE,
  TMAP19-008 (TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP), AND MITIGATED NEGATIVE
  DECLARATION AND MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING
  PROGRAM)
  APPLICANT: 1784 CAPITAL HOLDINGS, LLC.

  The proposed project is a 199,358 square foot building with self-storage and
  artist studio uses. The City Council considered this item at a public hearing on
  November 17, 2020. At the public hearing, the City Council discussed the
  proposed project, requested additional information, and continued this item
  to the December 15, 2020 City Council regular meeting.

  Recommended Action:

  The action of the City Council may be to approve, approve with modifications,
  or deny the Planned Development and Tentative Parcel Map. Staff
  recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss the proposed Ordinance;
  2. Motion to waive full reading and introduce the attached Ordinance. No.
  671 by title only. The City Clerk will read aloud the full title of the
  Ordinance.

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA, TO ADOPT A MITIGATED NEGATIVE
  DECLARATION AND MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING
  PROGRAM AND TO APPROVE PLANNING CASE NUMBERS ZC19-001
  AND TMAP19-008, A PLANNED DEVELOPMENT OVERLAY ZONE AND
  TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP FOR THE PROJECT AT 414-420 SOUTH SAN
  GABRIEL BOULEVARD

  3. Motion to approve the First Reading of Ordinance No. 671 and to waive
  future reading of the Ordinance; and
  4. Schedule the Second Reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 671 for the
  next regular City Council meeting. The Second Reading will require a
  majority vote of the total membership of the Council.

  City Council Options

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 15, 2020  5
   Should the City Council wish to take an alternative route, the following
  options may be considered:

  1. Continue this item to a date uncertain and require the applicant to
  enter into a Development Agreement (DA) with the City. The
  Development Agreement would be an opportunity for further
  negotiations with the applicant and will need to be reviewed and
  approved by the City Attorney’s Office. This item would be re-noticed
  for a future City Council meeting in accordance with the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code.
  2. Deny the proposed project.

  6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION TO APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 20-68, APPROVING A
  PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT WITH THE ALAMEDA CORRIDOR-
  EAST CONSTRUCTION AUTHORITY ON BEHALF OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS FOR REAL PROPERTY LOCATED AT
  405 SOUTH DEL MAR AVENUE

  Additional Attachment: Purchase and Sale Agreement

  At the conclusion of the Alameda Corridor East trench project in San Gabriel
  in August 2018, the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG)
  declared the property at 405 S. Del Mar as surplus property left over from the
  project. The City has been working with the SGVCOG to purchase the property
  for possible use as an affordable housing project. This item is to consider a
  Purchase and Sale Agreement (PSA) by and between the Alameda Corridor-
  East Construction Authority on behalf of the SGVCOG, and the City of San
  Gabriel.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council consider approval of Resolution No.
  20-68, approving the Purchase and Sale Agreement with the Alameda
  Corridor-East Construction Authority on behalf of the San Gabriel Valley
  Council of Governments for the purchase of the site at 405 S. Del Mar Avenue,
  and to authorize the City Manager to execute the PSA and any other
  documents related to the purchase.

  7. PUBLIC COMMENT

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – December 15, 2020  6
   8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members
  to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  The regularly-scheduled City Council meeting of January 5, 2021, has been
  cancelled. The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, January
  19, 2021, at 6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each
  meeting will be available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the
  City’s website at www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF DECEMBER 15, 2020
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:33 P.M. on Tuesday, December 15, 2020, with all Council Members and staff
  participating by teleconference.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  A. CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATORS (GOVERNMENT CODE
  SECTION 54956.8)

  B. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS (GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION
  54957.6)

  Assistant City Attorney Pilchen reported that in the Closed Session Special Meeting
  immediately preceding this meeting, direction was given to staff and no reportable
  action was taken on the listed items. He also reported that the Special Meeting would

I  be reconvened following this meeting for consideration of a third matter.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Harrington.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Jason Pu, Vice Mayor
  Chin Ho Liao, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City
  Manager/Community Development Director Armine
  Chaparyan, Assistant City Attorney Lloyd Pilchen,
  Community  Services/Interim  Mission  Playhouse
  Director Rebecca Perez, Police Chief Eugene Harris,
  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
  Engineer Greg de Vinck, Fire Chief Steven Wallace,
  Human Resources/Risk Management Director Edward

I  AN NOU NCEM ENTS
  Macias, and Interim Finance Director Kenneth Louie.

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 5  December 15, 2020
   Mayor Menchaca announced that staff had requested that item 4E, Award of
  Professiona l Service Agreement to North Star Land Care for Citywide Street Tree
  Ma intenance Services, be pulled from the Consent Calendar, to be considered at a
  later time.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Mayor Menchaca, to approve
  the agenda order as amended to remove item 4E.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

I  AYES:
  NOES:
  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. COVID-19 BRIEFING

  The presentation was made by Fire Chief Wallace, Police Chief Harris, and
  Assistant City Manager/Community Development Director Chaparyan.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Mario Pace, resident, provided comments expressing dissatisfaction with the
  notification for the Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission
  Subcommittee Meeting held on December 3, 2020.

I  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Liao, seconded by Council Member Pu, to approve
  Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4D and 4F - 4G as presented.

  Motion approved Consent Calendar Items 4A - 40 and 4F - 4G as presented by a vote
  of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following :

  1. M inutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of November 17, 2020.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of December 1, 2020.

I  3. M inutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of December 1, 2020.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved the November 19, 2020, and November 24, 2020,
  Registers of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT - NOVEMBER 2020

  CITY COUNC IL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 5  December 15, 2020
   The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for November
  2020.

  D. RESOLUTION NO. 20-66 ESTABLISHING CAMPAIGN CONTRIBUTION LIMITS
  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTIONS 85301AND83124

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 20-66 establishing campaign
  contribution limits pursuant to Government Code Sections 85301 and 83124.

I  E. AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICE AGREEMENT TO NORTH STAR LAND CARE
  FOR CITYWIDE STREET TREE MAINTENANCE SERVICES

  This item was pulled from the agenda and not considered.

  F. LEASE-PURCHASE OF A 2021 FORD F-150 PICK-UP TRUCK

  The City Council :
  1. Waived formal bidding and authorized the Cooperative Purchase Agreement
  consistent with the piggyback bidding requirements pursuant to Municipal
  Code Section 34.35.
  2. Authorized the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with National Auto
  Fleet Group in the amount not to exceed $28,466.48.

  G. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE

  The City Council received and filed the report.

I  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. 414-420 SOUTH SAN GABRIEL BOULEVARD PLANNING CASE NOS. ZC19-001
  (ZONE CHANGE/PLANNED DEVELOPMENT OVERLAY ZONE, TMAP19-008
  (TENTATIVE PARCEL MAP), AND MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION AND
  MITIGATION MONITORING AND REPORTING PROGRAM)
  APPLICANT: 1784 CAPITAL HOLDINGS, LLC.
  (CONTINUED FROM NOVEMBER 17, 2020)

  The staff presentation was made by Senior Planner Matt Chang.

  There was no public comment; therefore, Mayor Menchaca closed the public
  hearing.

  TLand-Use Consultant Shane Swerdlow of Craig Lawson & Co., LLC, representing
  the applicant, made a presentation and introduced project-team members.

  Discussion included methodology for calculating the estimated market demand;
  appreciation of the project elements and for the increased development impact

I  fees designated for the Police and Fire Departments; possible effects of this project
  on City image and on location desirability to other potential merchants; property
  and sales tax benefits to the City compared to other types of projects; trends
  related to self-storage in other cities; consideration of future programming for the
  entire corridor; and values for the property now and after the project is built.

  A motion was made by Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to waive
  full reading and introduce Ordinance. No. 671 by title only.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 5  December 15, 2020
   Chief City Clerk Clark read the title of Ordinance No. 671 into the record, "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, to Adopt a
  Mitigated Negative Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program
  and to Approve Planning Case Numbers ZC19-001 And TMAP19 -008, a Planned
  Development Overlay Zone and Tentative Parcel Map for the Project at 414-420
  South San Gabriel Boulevard."

  Motion carried by a vote of 4- 1 as follows:

I  AYES:

  DING, HARRINGTON, LIAO, MENCHACA
  PU
  NONE

  A motion was made by Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor Liao, to approve

  and to schedule the second reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 671 for the
  next regular City Council meeting.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4- 1 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  PU
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  6. NEW BUSINESS

I  A. CONSIDERATION TO APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 20-68, APPROVING A
  PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT WITH THE ALAMEDA CORRIDOR-
  EAST CONSTRUCTION AUTHORITY ON BEHALF OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  VALLEY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS FOR REAL PROPERTY LOCATED AT
  405 SOUTH DEL MAR AVENUE

  The presentation was made by Economic Development Manager Domenica
  Megerdichian and Assistant City Attorney Pilchen.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included the low cost for a property which will benefit the
  community with an affordable housing project, the need for as many affordable
  housing units as possible, and outreach to the community regarding the future
  proposed project.

  A motion was made by Council Member Pu, seconded by Council Member
  Ding, to adopt Resolution No. 20-68 approving the Purchase and Sale
  Agreement with the Alameda Corridor-East Construction Authority on behalf

I  of the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments for the purchase of the site
  at 405 S. Del Mar Avenue, and to authorize the City Manager to execute the
  PSA and any other documents related to the purchase.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HARRINGTON, PU, LIAO, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 5  December 15, 2020
   7. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  8. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto thanked Interim Finance Director Louie for his service during
  difficult times and wished him farewell; and commented on a street project that will
  repair 12 miles of residential streets in the City over the next month.

  Interim Finance Director Louie thanked the City Council and City Manager Lazzaretto

I  for the opportunity to serve the City of San Gabriel.

  9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Mayor Menchaca and Vice Mayor Liao commended Interim Finance Director Louie for
  a job well-done and wished him luck in his future endeavors.

  Council Member Pu thanked Interim Finance Director Louie; and reported on the
  Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission Subcommittee meeting and
  that options are being explored for the upcoming Lunar New Year Festival.

  Council Member Harrington thanked Interim Finance Director Louie for his service and
  wished all a Merry Christmas, Happy New Year, and happy holiday season.

  Council Member Ding thanked Interim Finance Director Louie for his service, gave a
  reminder to stay safe and stay home, and wished all a happy holiday and Happy New
  Year.

I  Mayor Menchaca reported on the Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR)
  Commission Subcommittee meeting; announced the Fire Department's Santa Drive-
  By Visit event; and wished everyone a Merry Christmas and to be safe and healthy.

  10.CLOSED SESSION - None.

  11. ADJOURNMENT

  Mayor Menchaca adjourned the meeting at 8:16 P.M.

  Respectfully submitted:

  Approved this 19th day of January, 2021 :

I
